title: Pinned runtime manifests for reproducible benchmark runs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Provide a canonical, pinned runtime manifest format and CI validators so benchmark and load-testing runs are reproducible across machines, runners, and CI agents. The manifest will include exact container image digests, GPU driver bundles (driver version + CUDA toolkit), runner binary SHA, kernel/driver flags, and a small canonical config for environment variables and mount points. This ticket covers the manifest schema, a reference generator tool, CI validators for PRs that change benchmark infra, and a short migration plan for existing benchmark jobs.
acceptance_criteria: A JSON/YAML manifest schema exists and is documented in Confluence with examples for A100-Linux and L4d (NVIDIA) nodes.
Reference generator (bench-manifest-gen) can emit manifests with image:tag@sha256 digests and driver bundles given a runner node type.
CI validator bot rejects PRs touching benchmark CI without an updated manifest or a documented compatibility rationale.
Perf runs executed with the pinned manifests produce token/sec and p95 numbers that match baseline within +/-2% in controlled envs.
Migration plan and rollout schedule published; at least two benchmark jobs converted to pinned manifests and validated in CI.
implementation_notes: Manifest fields: node_type, container_images (list of image@sha256), nvidia_driver_version, cuda_toolkit_version, runner_binary_sha, kernel_version, env_overrides, bind_mounts, mount_permissions, launch_args.
Store canonical manifests in /bench/manifests in the infra repo; name by node_type and date (e.g., a100-2025-02-01.yaml).

Add bench-manifest-gen binary to infra-tools; it will query GCR/ECR for latest digest for a given image tag and validate driver bundles via a small compatibility matrix maintained in drivers/compat.csv.

CI: new job bench/validate-manifest runs on PRs in infra/bench and benchmarks/bench-runs. It checks manifest schema, confirms referenced digests exist, and runs a lightweight smoke runner on a small VM to verify runner_binary_sha boots.
Metrics: extend benchmark runner to tag results with manifest_id; update the perf dashboard to allow filtering and grouping by manifest_id for regression detection.
test_plan: Unit tests for bench-manifest-gen to ensure digests are resolved and schema validation works.

End-to-end test: deploy pinned manifest on a canary node type (a100-canary), run 100 warmup requests + 1k measurement requests for the standard prompt set, compute tokens/sec and p95 and assert within baseline thresholds.
CI gating: failing manifest validation blocks merges to main for benchmark infra changes.
Load test reproducibility check: run two identical runs across different datacenters (us-west-2 and eu-west-1) with the same manifest and compare p95/token/sec deltas; document acceptable variance.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Pinning too strictly could block security updates (e.g., kernel patches). Mitigation: add a security-exempt label/process to allow documented, time-boxed exceptions and automatic refreshing of manifests after security fixes.

Risk: Operator burden of maintaining driver compatibility matrix. Mitigation: provide an automated probe tool that runs on any node type and reports compatibility results to a central drivers dashboard.
Risk: Different clouds/hardware expose subtle performance differences. Mitigation: require manifest_id tagging in dashboards and fold manifests into regression alerts to avoid false positives.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (1 week): Define schema and implement bench-manifest-gen. Convert 2 low-risk benchmark jobs (smoke and long-tail) to pinned manifests.
Phase 2 (2 weeks): Add CI manifest validation and convert critical benchmark jobs; run parallel comparisons between old and pinned runs for 1 week.
Phase 3 (ongoing): Require manifests for all new benchmark jobs; quarterly audit to refresh driver bundles and image digests with changelog.
